newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares seen near highs in '97-technical analysts.
newsitem.headline: KL shares seen near highs in '97-technical analysts.

text.p: Malaysia's surging stock market could test an all-time high before the end of 1997, technical analysts said.

"Providing the current trend holds, I expect the Composite Index to test the 1,330 area within the first quarter (of 1997)," said John Schofield, regional technical analyst at Nava SC Securities Research Ltd in Hong Kong.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index (CI) posted its highest close in almost three years last Wednesday when it ended at 1,254.42. The index was at 1,249.70 on Tuesday.
Analysts said the market can expect a record-breaking year.

"Based on recent volumes, the market has been at its best for the last two-and-a-half years. There has been a breakout triangle, which leads me to be bullish," said Fred Tam, managing director of technical analysis firm P.I. Capital Research Sdn Bhd in Kuala Lumpur.
"It should test 1,332 between now and early March," he added.
The CI hit an all-time high of 1,332.04 on January 4, 1994.
"Since then, the index has been on a long-term correction," said Nizam Idris, technical analyst at economic analysis group I.D.E.A. in Singapore.
Where Tam and Schofield differ, however, is in what happens after the CI sets a new all-time high.
Schofield said that if the record is broken convincingly the next "important" resistance level is not until 1,440.
But Tam feels the index will fall back after nearing the 1,332 level.
"I don't know whether it is likely to break this level. There could be a sharp correction after this, since around March we enter a bearish pattern," he said.
One possible reason why the market will be correcting around early March is a solar eclipse on March 9, according to Tam. "It could have negative repercussions on the stock market".
Some technical analysts in Malaysia are known to consult astronomical charts for hints on market movements and their subsequent predictions carry considerable weight with some investors.
Nizam, however, is convinced that investors will have to wait for a while longer before the all-time high is reached.
"I expect the market to be down from now on," he said. "I don't think it will hit the high this year."
"The most interesting feature of this market is that the rally has been supported, despite weakness in some large capitalised stocks like Telekom Malaysia and Petronas Gas," said Schofield.
Among the technically most attractive stocks are Malayan Banking Bhd, Proton Bhd, United Engineers Bhd and YTL Corp Bhd, he said.
"On a long-term basis, YTL shows one of the best trends of any stock," he added.
($1 = 2.49 ringgit)
